naya.summary: Today the Smart Notes architecture was materially upgraded from multiple flat legacy folders to a canonical event-centric chronological memory model. Twelve legacy source files were read and consolidated into ten Note Events, a canonical index and migration provenance were created, Constitution v3 and Bootstrap v3 were activated, a v3 runtime was added, and all five legacy folders were removed after migration verification.
wins: Naya/Human duplicate pairs were consolidated rather than duplicated.
Verification receipts are now constitutional law.
Daily Intelligence and CIS are explicitly part of the memory architecture.
learning: Time should organize memory while meaning retrieves it.
A Note Event is the correct primary object; Naya/Human are representations.
A receipt must be treated as part of the work, not a courtesy.
Architecture should distinguish design intent from implemented enforcement.
next_best_actions: Run Smart Notes v3 validation in an executable CI environment.
Implement semantic retrieval beyond lexical/alias matching.
Implement automatic duplicate detection and feed receipt integration.
Automate verified Daily/Weekly/Monthly CIS report generation.

human.summary: We cleaned up the old Smart Notes mess and moved the knowledge into one logical superbrain structure. The old Naya/Sean/Shawn/Smart Notes piles are gone. The new system is organized by time, connected by meaning, and designed to prove that notes were actually saved. The next step is hardening the automation so the architecture enforces itself instead of relying on documentation alone.

evidence: Migration manifest records 12 legacy files mapped into 10 canonical events.
Legacy source directories returned 404 after deletion, confirming the old folder paths no longer exist.
Canonical event index and Constitution v3 were committed.
v3 runtime and bootstrap were committed.
